slot.subtopic: Active and passive voice - complex sentences
slot.brief: Convert a sentence with two clauses and mixed tenses (one passive clause in past perfect) into active voice; watch tricky verb forms and pronoun shifts.

stem: Change into active voice: The committee was informed by the secretary that the revised schedule had been approved by the chair before the delegates arrived.
options: The chair informed the secretary that the committee had approved the revised schedule before the delegates arrived.
The secretary had informed the committee that the chair approved the revised schedule before the delegates arrived.
The secretary informed the committee that the chair had approved the revised schedule before the delegates arrived.
The secretary informed the committee that the chair has approved the revised schedule before the delegates arrived.

verdicts.working: Change the main clause to active: “The secretary informed the committee.” Change the subordinate clause to active: “the chair had approved the revised schedule.”

working:
“Was informed” → “informed”; “had been approved” → “had approved.” The simple past in “arrived” remains unchanged.

Independent check: Change the main clause to active: “The secretary informed the committee.” Change the subordinate clause to active: “the chair had approved the revised schedule.”
solution: The passive “was informed by the secretary” becomes the active “the secretary informed.” In the subordinate clause, “had been approved by the chair” becomes “the chair had approved”; “arrived” remains unchanged. Thus, the sentence matches option (C).
